\section*{Test sheet: drafts of the letters missing in the non-regular styles}
To-do item: ``Create the glyphs that are missing in the non-regular styles because the base groups now reach further than the designer's coverage (Ɇ Ɍ Ɏ ɏ ꝥ ꞓ Ɱ ꭒ ỿ exist only in regular, Ɉ ẜ ẝ not in every style, and Ɋ Ỻ Ⅎ before them), as stage 2 already does for a few.'' BASE\_IPA has no gaps; these 15 letters of BASE\_LATIN are all.

\smallskip Drafts are in \textcolor{draft}{blue}; black is the designer's glyph. The drafts are in \verb|fonts/*-draft.otf| (the patched fonts plus the drafts; no anchors), written by \verb|run_missing_glyphs_sheet.py|; the recipes are in \verb|missing_glyphs.py|. Each letter is drafted from the style's own letters where the regular glyph shows how the designer built it:
\begin{description}\setlength\itemsep{0pt}\small
\item[Method (rebuilt 2026-11-13)] Every draft is built from components, as a font source builds a glyph: the base letter's own contours, plus a part that is a glyph of the font or one simple contour, or a splice of two contours. No boolean operations: the drafts keep the components' own points and \emph{overlap} where the components overlap (FontForge shows them unmerged; font generation merges them). In regular the designer built most of these letters the same way: Ɇ\,=\,E\,+\,U+0338 (0.2\,\% mismatch), Ɍ\,=\,R\,+\,U+0335, ẝ\,=\,ſ\,+\,U+0335, Ɉ\,=\,J\,+\,U+0336, …
\item[overlay] Ɍ Ɏ ɏ ẝ ꞓ ỻ: the base and the style's own stroke overlay mark (U+0335 or U+0336), scaled to the bar's length and the style's bar thickness (own Đ, Ƚ or đ), placed as the mark fits in the designer's glyph: its height, and its offset from the stem (or the de-slanted centre).
\item[reference] Ɇ: E and the long solidus U+0338 (redrawn in semibold and semibold italic, where it was the short one), crossing half E's height 23 left of E's de-slanted centre. Ỻ: I, L and a bar contour. Ⅎ Ɐ Ʌ: turned references.
\item[part] ẜ ꝥ: the base and the stroke of regular's glyph as one contour (ẜ's a rectangle, ꝥ's with its swelling ends), slanted and thickened to the style.
\item[splice] Ɱ (M and J's hook), ꭒ (u and ɿ's fishhook), ỿ (y and regular's ỿ loop), ɋ (q's own descender and ʈ's hook, regular ɽ's, at the descender), Ɉ (italic J, its own crossbar spliced out, + U+0336), Ɋ (regular's Ɋ, its bowl spliced from the style's O, its tail lengthened by splicing it with itself moved down): the outlines are cut where they cross a line and joined there; points left on a straight edge are dropped.
\end{description}
Each cell shows the base letter, the letter, and a letter of the same style with the analogous part. Comparison rows: Gentium Plus, Noto Serif and Junicode (the medievalist font, for ẜ ẝ ꝥ ỿ Ỻ ỻ Ⅎ); Langscitinus is left out because it has exactly Libertinus's gaps. A dash: the font lacks the letter.

\section*{Control points of the grafts}
The drafts as compiled into \verb|fonts/*-draft.otf| (what FontForge shows on opening them): on-curve points black, off-curve points as open circles on their handles; the dashed line is the joining height (on the designer's regular glyph, where the recipe joins when it is run in regular). The outlines are the result of a boolean union and cut (skia-pathops); at the join, points left on a straight stem are dropped, so a stem runs straight from the base letter's line into the donor's, as in regular Ɱ.\par\medskip

\section*{Recipe checks in regular}
The recipes that take a part from another letter, run in regular and compared with the designer's glyph (in the regular draft font at U+F600 and up). Mismatch: the ink of designer XOR recipe, at the same origin, over the designer's ink; a shift of the whole letter counts double on a thin letter (once where ink is missing, once where it is extra), so the mismatch after the best horizontal shift is given too.\par
